content.text:
What kind of story is Swan Lake?

Swan Lake is the love story of Princess Odette — a swan by day and a maiden by night — and Prince Siegfried. Woven from the world's finest ballet, composed by Tchaikovsky, this storybook shares the meaning of true love alongside beautiful music.

content.text:
The original story of Swan Lake

Swan Lake is a ballet composed by Tchaikovsky (1840-1893) in 1875-1876 and first performed in 1877 at the Bolshoi Theatre in Moscow. The premiere was poorly received, but a re-choreographed version in 1895 was a great success, making it the most frequently performed ballet in the world today. The original has two endings — one tragic and one happy.

content.text:
Plot summary of Swan Lake

Prince Siegfried sees swans turning into maidens by the lakeside and falls in love with Princess Odette. Through the sorcerer Rothbart's scheme, the prince mistakes the disguised Odile for Odette, but he realizes his mistake, races back, and pours out his true heart. Their love overcomes the magic, and Odette becomes human forever.

content.alt: Swan Lake - The lesson it teaches
content.text:
The lesson Swan Lake teaches

The heart of the story is that true love overcomes any darkness, and we should look at the heart rather than being fooled by appearances. You can also talk together about the courage it takes to admit a mistake and protect your love.

content.alt: Swan Lake - How to read it aloud
content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Play Tchaikovsky's original music in the background, and read Odette brightly, Rothbart gloomily, and Odile with a subtle difference. Talk about the importance of seeing the heart with, "They look exactly alike — how can we tell them apart?" It's well suited to ages 5-7.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is Swan Lake best for?
A. It's well suited to ages 5-7. Enjoying it alongside ballet and music can nurture an artistic sensibility as well.

Q. Is it a fairy tale or a ballet?
A. It's originally Tchaikovsky's ballet, with its story woven into a storybook. It's even better read with the music.

Q. What activities pair well with it?
A. Mimicking a swan dance while listening to the ballet music, a game of telling Odette and Odile apart, and drawing a favorite scene are all great.
